what_this_file_is: The four known-false objects of the review plan's proves_too_much block, each executed against its declared failure signature. Objects 1 and 2 re-execute the producer's machinery AND carry an independent re-derivation; objects 3 and 4 had not been run in this form by the producer. A control passing means the machinery FAILED where its conclusion is false, which is the required outcome. It is not evidence that the algorithm works.
how_object_4_was_run: joint_balance.log2_solve_cost was rebound IN MEMORY inside the validator's own script; the file on disk is unchanged and its committed sha256 still verifies.

objects.known_false_conclusion: the chained-S_3 algorithm beats van Oorschot-Wiener parallel rho at n = 163
objects.why_known_false: Semaev's own Table 3 prints stage-1 cost above 2^{n/2} at every n it lists below 300 (n = 100, 150, 200, 250 as printed).
objects.declared_failure_signature: Semaev LOSES under every metric and both storage readings

detail.independent_check_on_the_printed_table: Every Table 3 row with n < 300 (n = 100, 150, 200, 250) has log2 of the printed stage-1 column strictly above n/2, recomputed here from the transcribed table. 4/4.
detail.note: The margins agree with COST-SEMBIN-8d123b's n = 163 row to the last printed digit, which is replication of the producer's code rather than an independent derivation; the Table 3 direction check is independent.

objects.object: eq. (4), the unchained single summation polynomial S_{m+1}
objects.known_false_conclusion: eq. (4) is competitive with the chained system
objects.why_known_false: The paper's entire contribution (Sections 2, 3, 4) is that the chain replaces one high-degree equation with t-1 equations of F_2-degree 3; if eq. (4) were competitive there would be no paper.
objects.declared_failure_signature: the same cost machinery must report eq. (4) catastrophically worse
objects.outcome: PASS -- required signature observed, under a reading MORE generous to eq. (4) than the producer's

detail.independent_derivation: From Section 4.5: eq. (4) Weil-descends to n Boolean equations in m*k variables of total F_2-degree at most m(m-1), with first fall degree bounded by m^2 + 1 (attributed there to [11]). The chain solves at degree <= 4 in (m-2)n + km variables under Assumption 1. Widths compared as log2 of the degree-bounded Boolean monomial count.
detail.why_more_generous: The producer's control charged eq. (4) at degree 2^{m-1}. This derivation charges it at the FIRST FALL degree m^2 + 1, which at m = 11 is 122 rather than 1024 -- the cheapest reading the frozen text supports. eq. (4) is still catastrophically worse, so the control's teeth do not depend on the harsher degree.
detail.what_a_failing_eq4_control_would_look_li: It would require eq. (4)'s degree-bounded width to come within a factor of the chain's, i.e. the m^2+1 (or 2^{m-1}) degree bound in m*k variables to be no larger than degree 4 in (m-2)n+km variables. That happens only when m is O(1) and n is small -- at m = 3, n = 21 the gap is already 30 bits. So this control cannot fail at cryptographic parameters, and its 328-1257 bit margin means it detects only a machinery that has lost the degree dependence entirely (e.g. a hard-coded degree, or a width function ignoring its degree argument). That is a real but narrow fault class, and the control should be read as a smoke test rather than as a bias detector.
detail.residual_gap: This does NOT discharge the prime-field nearby-object control that protocol_deviations D1 records as owed. eq. (4) is a member of the same family as the object under test and cannot detect a bias shared by the family. Adequacy of that substitution is J6, which this task does not own.

objects.object: FREE-YIELD NULL -- eq. (11)'s probability set to 1, so decomposition never fails
objects.known_false_conclusion: charging a free lunch makes the attack worse
objects.why_known_false: Removing a cost can only make an algorithm cheaper. In eq. (15) the factor 1/P is exactly m! * 2^{n-mk}, since Section 4.5.2 substitutes P ~ 2^{mk-n}/m!; deleting it leaves stage 1 = 2^k * n^{4w}.
objects.declared_failure_signature: the crossover in n must DECREASE, or stay equal, never increase
objects.what_it_detects: an inverted sign convention shared by both implementations, which no amount of agreement between memory_charged_cost.py and independent_arith.py could catch
objects.outcome: PASS -- the crossover moved DOWN in 16/16 CLAIM A cells and 3/3 CLAIM B readings; no cell moved up or stayed equal

claim_A.m_policy_reoptimised: m re-minimised under the free-yield stage-1 cost; the free-yield objective is monotone decreasing in k, so it saturates at the sweep's m ceiling of 30
claim_A.m_policy_eq11_argmin: m held at eq. (11)'s own argmin, which isolates the yield term

detail.bonus_finding: Re-running the producer's crossover scan over a WIDER window (n in [150, 900] rather than the record's [250, 650]) returned 303, 375 and 435 unchanged. The three headline crossovers are therefore not artifacts of the sweep window.

objects.object: solving cost made EXPONENTIAL in (m - t): log2 solve = base(t = m*) - rate * k * (m* - t)
objects.why_known_false: Under a model in which each unit of chain shortening saves rate*k bits and the yield loss per unit is only about k - log2 t bits, shortening MUST pay once rate exceeds 1.
objects.declared_failure_signature: t_star < m_star; if the optimizer still returns t* = m* it is not optimizing over t and CLAIM B is vacuous
objects.outcome: PASS -- the optimizer returns t* = 2 < m* at every tested n once the rate exceeds the yield-loss rate, and the transition sits exactly at the predicted threshold

detail.threshold_is_the_predicted_one: The flip occurs between rate 0.9k and 1.0k. The independently derived yield loss per unit of t is k - log2 t bits, so the break-even rate is just under 1.0 * k. Agreement to within one grid step means the optimizer is not merely varying t, it is trading t off against the yield term with the correct sensitivity.
detail.conclusion_on_J4c: The optimizer genuinely sweeps t. The record's known_false_t_independent_solve control (which forces t* = m* via Semaev's own t-free n^{4w} reading) could indeed have passed for a trivial reason; this object rules that out. CLAIM B's t* = m* is a computed result, not a fixed point of a bug.

additional_control_the_run_does_not_have.name: sign-of-the-measured-tradeoff positive control
additional_control_the_run_does_not_have.why: Section 3 step 3 asserts that solving time 'drops dramatically' for t < m, and Table 2 is the only published measurement of that tradeoff. A cost model that returns t* = m* everywhere must nonetheless AGREE with the measurement at the parameters where it was made, or it is inconsistent with the paper's own data.
additional_control_the_run_does_not_have.procedure: Evaluate the producer's macaulay4 model at the five Table 2 parameter sets that carry t < m rows, and compare the model's argmin over t against the measured expected cost per relation (avg_seconds / P_theoretical).
additional_control_the_run_does_not_have.outcome: PASS on sign, 5/5. The model says t < m pays at every parameter set where the paper measured it, and the paper's own numbers say the same. This is the one place where CLAIM B's model can be checked against data, and it is checked in the direction that could have falsified it.
additional_control_the_run_does_not_have.magnitude_caveat: The model OVERSTATES the size of the short-chain gain at these parameters -- 36.4 bits predicted against 15.0 bits measured at (n, m) = (15, 5). The bias is toward finding an interior optimum, so a model biased toward t < m still returning t* = m* at n >= 250 is a one-sided robustness statement in CLAIM B's favour. It says nothing about whether the magnitude extrapolates.

summary.what_this_does_not_establish: Four passing known-false controls establish that the cost machinery is not degenerate in four specific ways. They do not establish that the accounting is the right accounting, that Assumption 1 holds, that eq. (11) describes realized yield, or that any curve is affected. A control that fails where its conclusion is false is the minimum bar, not evidence of correctness.
